plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30% of the book, to favor income and broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and concentrating in income/broad index. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%, MUU to 3%, and METU to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Buy MSFT, targeting 4% of the book, to add a high-quality tech name from the scanner.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some exposure to high-quality tech.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index with quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to SOXL, MUU, METU, and SPAL, targeting 7%, 6%, 6%, and 6% respectively, to lean into leveraged ETFs.
Buy MSFT, targeting 6% of the book, to add a high-scoring quality tech name.
This plan stretches for growth by using and adding leveraged ETFs and concentrating in strong setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases both upside and drawdown potential due to higher leverage and concentration in volatile assets. Be aware of daily decay/rebalancing in leveraged ETFs and the potential for rapid, substantial losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30% of the book, to favor income and broad index exposure.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
